newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish coalition experts back govt tax proposals.
newsitem.headline: Polish coalition experts back govt tax proposals.

text.p: A group of experts has backed a plan by Poland's ruling leftist coalition for moderate tax cuts, government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Monday.
"The conclusions of this team are such that practically speaking only the government proposals, presented in the Sejm (lower house) by the Prime Minister are acceptable," she told a news conference.

The group was set up by the government to examine tax proposals ahead of a key Senate vote. The government proposed late last month to cut personal income taxes to 20, 31 and 43 percent from the present 21, 33 and 45 percent respectively.

But in a surprise for the government the Sejm backed an opposition bill introducing a four-level tax scale with a new low 17-percent band which the government argues would boost the defict to unacceptable levels or require spending cuts.

The Senate is due to vote on the tax bill on November 13-14 and Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko has said he would try to persuade the coalition members to reject the lower house's bill and back the government proposals.
Jakubowska said the two coalition parties -- the Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) -- would meet later on Monday to discuss the experts' recommendations. @

Shortly after the vote the PSL, whose deputies backed opposition proposals, have signalled they might withdraw their support for the four tax bands if they were persuaded that the plan was economically unfeasible.
But the Peasants have said they might seek a deeper cut in the lowest tax rate to 19 percent rather than the 20 percent envisaged by the finance ministry.
